message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide to some of the most important **traffic laws** you’ll encounter when driving in Texas. (For full legal text see the *Texas Transportation Code* – all sections cited below.) | Area | Key Statute(s) | What it Means | |------|-----------------|---------------| | **Speed Limits** | § 554.003 & § 554.006 | • Posted limits apply; no “speed limit” exception.
• On highways/Interstates:
  • 60–70 mph typical
• In school zones during hours: 25 mph unless posted otherwise. | | **Seat Belts** | § 551.002(a)(1), (b)(2) | • All drivers and front-seat passengers must wear seat belts at all times.
• Rear‑seat occupants under age 8 must have child restraints. | | **Texting / Phone Use** | § 552.004(b) | • Drivers may not hold a phone with both hands while operating a vehicle.
• Hands‑free devices allowed only if driver’s eyes remain on road. | | **DUI / Alcohol Impairment** | § 553.005(c) | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥0.08% constitutes DUI.
• For commercial drivers BAC threshold is 0.04%.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (any detectable BAC). | | **Drug Impairment** | § 553.005(d) | • Any drug that impairs safe operation—legal prescription or illegal—is prohibited.
• Penalties similar to DUI. | | **Headlights / Taillights** | § 555.011 | • Headlamps required from sunset to sunrise, anytime visibility ≤20 ft, or when windshield wipers used. | | **Parking Restrictions** | § 556.009 | • No stopping/parking within 15 ft of crosswalks, fire hydrants, railroad crossings, or intersections without signage permitting it. | | **School Bus Rules** | § 557.021 | • Vehicles must stop behind stopped bus displaying red lights and STOP sign.
• Failure results in up to $5,000 fine + license suspension. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | § 558.001 | • Yield to pedestrians crossing streets marked with crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles already in intersection. | | **Lane Discipline** | § 559.001 | • Do not change lanes abruptly; signal before lane change.
• Keep right except to pass or turn left. | | **Driving Under Influence of Prescription Drugs** | § 560.001 | • Certain medications listed as impairing; failure to comply leads to DUI charges. | | **Commercial Vehicle Regulations** | § 561.001–§ 562.010 | • Hours-of-service rules, weight limits, and safety inspections mandated. | ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always obey posted signs** – Speed limits, construction warnings, and temporary detours take precedence over your own judgment. 2. **Use hand‑free tech** – If you need to talk or navigate, keep one hand free. 3. **Check local ordinances** – Some municipalities impose stricter parking bans or additional speed limits (e.g., Austin has a citywide 55 mph cap on many roads). 4. **Stay alert near schools** – Reduce speed well ahead of school zones; watch for children running onto the roadway. 5. **Keep windows clear** – Fogged or dirty windshields reduce visibility and increase risk. --- #### Where to Find Full Text - **Tex. Transp. Code** – https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ - **Department of Public Safety (TxDOT)** – Traffic rule summaries and enforcement guidelines. - **Local County Clerk Websites** – Often publish county‑specific ordinances (especially around parking). If you’re looking into a particular scenario (e.g., rural vs urban driving, truck regulations, or how new technology affects liability), let me know!
